repo_notes.content: Footnote is a transparency- and provenance-focused AI framework. Its main product feature is inspectability: users should be able to see why an answer was produced, not just the answer itself.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Keep the landing page polished and curated. The Introduction page should feel editorial, not like a raw index dump, and it should explain how to navigate the rest of the wiki in plain language.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Use short menu titles wherever possible. Put nuance into purpose statements and page notes instead of long navigation labels.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Keep the wiki flow-first and junior-friendly. Prefer explaining one request moving through the system over listing isolated modules.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Repeat the package boundary rule throughout the wiki: web and discord-bot should integrate through backend HTTP APIs, not direct runtime imports from backend internals.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Structure pages around Purpose, Key concepts, Ownership boundaries, Typical flow, Failure modes, How to test, and Related pages. For routes and data flows, add a concrete How it works walkthrough.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Treat docs freshness as part of the contract. If a PR changes route shapes, runtime schemas, provenance fields, trace behavior, or user-visible feature flows, update the matching canonical Markdown page in the same PR. Edit this DeepWiki configuration only when its structure, material source entrypoints, or durable generation guidance changes.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Keep this file within Footnote's operating target of no more than 28 pages and 90 total notes. The hard validation limits remain 30 pages and 100 notes across repo_notes and every page_notes array; headroom warnings should leave room for future durable updates.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Use screenshots selectively on user-facing pages such as Discord and Web features. One or two tightly cropped images are enough when they make the feature easier to understand.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Explain prompt setup in plain language: use shared core instructions plus one persona at a time. If multiple persona env settings are present, apply them in this order: `BOT_PROFILE_PROMPT_OVERLAY`, then `BOT_PROFILE_PROMPT_OVERLAY_PATH`, then the default persona.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Explain that TRACE metadata is built by backend code and API annotations, not by assistant-written message text.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

repo_notes.content: Document the runtime boundary clearly: backend owns the public chat contract, provenance, and traces, while `@footnote/agent-runtime` owns the replaceable execution layer. VoltAgent is the active text runtime.
repo_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Introduction
pages.purpose: Welcome a new contributor with a polished overview of what Footnote is, why provenance matters, how the wiki is organized, and what to read first.

page_notes.content: Use this as the curated landing page. Include sections for what Footnote is, why it is different, how to read the wiki, a first-30-minutes walkthrough, and suggested reading paths.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Start here, then read Architecture, Glossary, and Provenance. Use Packages when you want to find where a feature lives in code. Include a simple first-run path: start the backend, open the web app, trigger one live chat request, and inspect the resulting trace. Keep this distinct from the homepage's checked-in prepared examples, which do not call a model.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Foundations
pages.purpose: Group the shared ideas that apply across the whole product: architecture, vocabulary, trace flow, provenance, and observability.

page_notes.content: Read this after Introduction. Keep it concept-first and save detailed feature tours for the Packages branch of the wiki.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain Footnote's durable system shape: backend-owned execution and public APIs, replaceable runtime adapters, shared contracts, and client boundaries.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: Use this as the system map. Contracts define shared serializable shapes, backend owns execution and validation, and web and Discord integrate through backend HTTP APIs.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: The backend composes runtime adapters behind provider-agnostic interfaces. Runtime adapters do not own public response acceptance, review, termination, provenance, auth, or cost authority.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: Prompt resolution starts with shared defaults, applies optional configuration overrides, then selects one active persona overlay.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Define the main Footnote terms in one place so the rest of the wiki stays easy to read.

page_notes.content: Include provenance, evidence/freshness scores, risk tier, tradeoff count, citations, chain hash, stale-after behavior, trace retrieval, and trace display.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Also define: workflow behavior presets (balanced/grounded), shared reviewed workflow shape (generate -> assess -> planner re-entry -> generate), assess decision signals (`reviewDecision`, `reviewReason`, and revise-only `revisionInstruction`), workflow plan step (workflow-owned planner timing/lineage), applied plan state (`AppliedPlanState`), plan continuation (`PlanContinuation`), context step (integration context injection before generation), planner advisory boundary (planner suggests, backend policy decides), planner result applier (policy-application seam), terminal_action (workflow terminal outcome for ignore/react/image).
page_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Provenance
pages.purpose: Explain why Footnote is different: answers are designed to be inspectable, traceable, and understandable to users.

page_notes.content: Explain both product meaning and engineering shape, then point readers to Trace Flow for the concrete end-to-end walkthrough.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Workflow
pages.purpose: Document workflow behavior presets, shared workflow shape, engine behavior, and where planner and context steps fit into the execution path.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: balanced and grounded presets use the shared reviewed workflow shape (generate -> assess -> planner re-entry -> generate).

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: workflowEngine owns step timing and lineage, not provider policy. The engine decides step legality, enforces limits, and records termination reasons.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: Planner runs as an early workflow `plan` step through injected `PlannerStepExecutor`, and workflow-owned plan lineage is the canonical source.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: Planner output remains advisory. Policy application runs outside workflowEngine through `PlannerResultApplier` + `PlanContinuationBuilder` before continuation (`terminal_action` or `continue_message`).

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: Context-step integrations include weather_forecast, web_search, file_scan, trustgraph, and reverse_image_search.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: TRACE alignment flows through assess lineage signals and runtime finalization, with target/final comparison semantics normalized via shared contracts helpers and canonical axis keys.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: Explain workflow step signals as small public clues for lineage and receipts, not raw prompts, model output, or broad telemetry. Known groups live in shared contracts, backend code emits them through builders, and consumers use shared readers instead of magic keys.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: Signal readers are intentionally cautious. Missing or malformed values should produce simple answers like false or null, while the public signal bag remains open for future primitive fields.

pages.title: Context Integrations
pages.purpose: Document how Footnote brings external context into workflows without giving integrations policy authority.

page_notes.content: weather_forecast is implemented as a workflow context-step integration and can inject context into the generation prompt.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: web_search is implemented as a workflow context-step integration. Keep provider protocol/tool semantics at runtime boundaries only.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: TrustGraph executes as a workflow context-step integration while keeping predicate/provenance mapping as a separate governance pass.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: reverse_image_search executes as an advisory workflow context-step integration for image attachments with non-blocking degradation behavior.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Search discovery is distinct from source reading. Discovery provides candidate sources; reading and citing sources is a later, stronger step.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Repository context selection and preview use `.footnote/context-files` plus `pnpm context:repo:list`; loading those files into TrustGraph is not implemented yet. Keep indexing support separate from the workflow context-step integration and from runtime authority.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Project Context
pages.purpose: Explain how Footnote answers questions about itself from approved project documents and a limited live GitHub view, while keeping source status, citations, and failure behavior visible.

page_notes.content: Start with the difference between the two sources. `project_context` reads approved local documents for Footnote explanations and discovery. `github_context` retrieves a limited live view of repository state.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Only files allowed by `.footnote/context-files` can be read. Footnote reads each selected document from one Git commit and cites an excerpt only with a link pinned to that commit. It never replaces a missing citation with a moving branch link.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Project documents and GitHub results are source material, not instructions. They cannot select policy, routing, credentials, verification, or when execution ends. Explain this in plain language before the prompt and workflow details.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Show failure behavior clearly: chat continues without project documents when a lookup fails, can use a last good index marked `stale`, and reports `partial` or `unavailable` source status in response metadata.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

page_notes.content: Include the deployment path. `pnpm context:bundle` packages approved documents from a commit for the server image; Docker receives that commit as a build argument. Project context is disabled by default, and its embedding provider is configured separately from chat.
page_notes.author: Maintainer

pages.title: Account Access
pages.purpose: Explain provider-neutral account sign-in and the separate backend authorization boundary for administrator settings.

page_notes.author: Maintainer
page_notes.content: OIDC proves provider identity; backend policy separately authorizes administrator settings. Sessions use opaque local state, provider tokens are not retained, and disabling sign-in leaves public Footnote running.
